prompt: Compare the apparent surface gloss of the two objects. Which object looks glossier? Judge gloss, not overall brightness. Answer exactly A if Image A looks glossier, B if Image B looks glossier, or SAME if their surface gloss looks indistinguishable.
system: You are a visual observer performing a surface-gloss matching task. Follow the response format exactly.
sampling: All 3888 images; shuffled matching-heldout images first; 39 development/practice images flagged separately; 72-image blocks, two randomized sessions per block
presentation: two original 512-square images in ordered placeholders, A=test and B=reference, each encoded to one 448 tile; no literal mouse slider; fresh context each decision
controller: Independent uniform start 2..51, then bisection over remaining integer interval; unchanged pilot stopping and conversion rules
scope: Frozen-protocol model adaptation with reconstructed references; matching-heldout validation, not exact reproduction of human apparatus
development_reason: v1 adjustment wording passed 3/9 reference-only controls; this exact direct-comparison wording passed 9/9. Same images and initial levels; no selection by human correlations.
starts: independent uniform integers 2..51 in both sessions
paper_adaptations: 72 unique images per computational block, no original 12 common human-observer items
three practice trials at run start and one no-image catch per session
two ordered 448px encoded images; deterministic fresh-context comparisons
bisection rather than mouse adjustment; crossing threshold rather than explicit equal-gloss match
no human monitor adaptation or reaction-time exclusion
reconstructed v3 references; not identical author stimuli
catch_instruction: No stimulus images are shown in this attention check. Move the reference slider to its LEFTMOST endpoint. The allowed indices are 1 to 52. Return only the selected index.
checkpoints: Every completed 72-image block; first 360 images are an interim checkpoint; continue full schedule regardless of correlation
primary_analysis: Heldout image-level Spearman human vs mean of two model matching estimates; bootstrap by image and separately by shape/illumination
secondary_analysis: comparison to existing single-image scores on identical images
